import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Preprocessing for visualization:
# Handle the 'Sleep Disorder' NaN values - replace with 'No Disorder' (if it were used in the plot)
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Ensure BMI Category order for better visualization
# Define a desired order for BMI categories
bmi_category_order = ['Underweight', 'Normal', 'Normal-Weight', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
# Filter the order to only include categories actually present in the data
actual_bmi_categories = [cat for cat in bmi_category_order if cat in df['BMI Category'].unique()]
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=actual_bmi_categories, ordered=True)

# Set a style for the plots for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create an insightful visualization:
# Explore the relationship between Sleep Duration, Quality of Sleep, and Stress Level,
# with Physical Activity Level influencing point size, and faceted by BMI Category.
# This reveals how sleep metrics and their relation to stress might differ based on BMI and activity.

g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Sleep Duration",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="Stress Level",      # Color points by Stress Level
    size="Physical Activity Level", # Size points by Physical Activity Level
    col="BMI Category",      # Create separate columns for each BMI Category
    col_wrap=2,              # Wrap columns after 2 plots for better layout
    palette="viridis",       # Colormap for Stress Level (sequential for ordinal data)
    sizes=(50, 400),         # Range of point sizes for Physical Activity Level
    height=4,                # Height of each facet
    aspect=1.2,              # Aspect ratio of each facet
    alpha=0.7,               # Transparency of points
    edgecolor="w",           # White edge for points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5,           # Line width of point edges
    kind="scatter"           # Specify scatter plot
)

# Set titles and labels
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)")
g.set_titles("BMI Category: {col_name}")
g.fig.suptitle("Sleep Health: Duration & Quality by Stress, Activity, and BMI", y=1.02, fontsize=16) # Main title for the figure

# Adjust legend placement for clarity
# relplot automatically creates a combined legend for hue and size.
# Place it outside the grid of plots to prevent overlap.
g.add_legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5), loc='center left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to make space for the legend and prevent labels/titles from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.98, 1]) # rect adjusts the plot area to leave space on the right for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
